section_summary: Pages 141–189 chiefly record U.S. inquiries into Japanese gold shipments to Latin America and Haiti in 1941, with negative reports from most posts and further questions about Brazil and Peru. Pages 190–197 concern the design of military currency for Japanese-controlled areas. The final pages address Japanese occupation currency in Netherlands New Guinea, guilder exchange arrangements, and a request to let U.S. personnel retain small amounts of Japanese currency.

subfiles.title: Charge slip
subfiles.about: File 894.515 circulation record.
subfiles.summary: Charge slip for the file, with largely illegible annotations.

subfiles.title: Quito telegram 455
subfiles.about: Gold imports from Japan into Ecuador.
subfiles.summary: No Japanese gold had entered through customs; Ecuadorian officials would report suspicious transactions.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Quito telegram 455
subfiles.about: Ecuadorian checks on Japanese gold and exchange transactions.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrases the report of no gold imports and limited funds available to the Japanese Legation.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Quito telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards the Quito telegram paraphrase.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the paraphrase of telegram 455.

subfiles.title: Montevideo telegram 434
subfiles.about: Gold shipments from Japan to Uruguay.
subfiles.summary: Reports none recently; remaining trade is chiefly barter under a clearing agreement.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Montevideo telegram
subfiles.about: Uruguayan gold imports and trade with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Restates that no recent gold shipments were found and trade was nearly paralyzed.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Montevideo telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards the Montevideo telegram paraphrase.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a paraphrase concerning Japanese gold imports to Uruguay.

subfiles.title: Port-au-Prince telegram 216
subfiles.about: Gold shipments from Japan to Haiti.
subfiles.summary: Reports that Haiti received no such shipments.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Port-au-Prince telegram
subfiles.about: Japanese gold shipments to Haiti.
subfiles.summary: Restates that no shipments were received.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Haiti telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards the Haiti telegram paraphrase.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the paraphrase of telegram 216.

subfiles.title: Rio de Janeiro telegram 1769
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Rio de Janeiro; Caffery
subfiles.about: Possible Japanese gold shipments to Brazil.
subfiles.summary: The Bank of Brazil knew of none, although the Yokohama Specie Bank had earlier discussed safekeeping shipments.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Rio telegram 1769
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Rio de Janeiro; Caffery
subfiles.about: Brazilian inquiry into Japanese gold.
subfiles.summary: Restates the Bank of Brazil’s denial and the earlier, apparently unpursued safekeeping proposal.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Rio telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards Rio telegram 1769.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the paraphrase and cites the earlier Rio report.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Toa Maru inquiry
subfiles.about: Whether to send a further inquiry about gold on the Toa Maru.
subfiles.summary: Says Rio already checked the ship’s unloading and found no gold.

subfiles.title: Draft inquiry to Rio about Toa Maru
subfiles.about: Reported discharge of two million dollars in gold in Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Draft asks the Embassy to verify a confidential report concerning the Toa Maru.

subfiles.title: Treasury copy of Rio transmittal
subfiles.about: Forwards Rio telegram 1769.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate transmittal with a Treasury circulation list.

subfiles.title: Treasury copy of Rio telegram paraphrase
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Rio de Janeiro; Caffery
subfiles.about: Bank of Brazil’s knowledge of Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate paraphrase reporting no known shipments and an earlier safekeeping inquiry.

subfiles.title: Panama telegram 437
subfiles.about: Japanese gold and merchant funds in Panama.
subfiles.summary: Finds no gold shipments; reports closure of Japanese businesses and a merchant’s $80,000 transfer to Peru.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Panama telegram
subfiles.about: Japanese gold and commercial activity in Panama.
subfiles.summary: Restates the lack of gold evidence and the Japanese merchant’s transfer to Lima.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Panama telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards the Panama telegram paraphrase.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the paraphrase of telegram 437.

subfiles.title: Mexico City telegram 644
subfiles.about: Japanese gold shipments to Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Bank inquiries found no recent shipments.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Mexico City telegram
subfiles.about: Mexican banks’ checks for Japanese gold.
subfiles.summary: Restates the negative findings of the Bank of Mexico and private banks.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Mexico telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards the Mexico City telegram paraphrase.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the paraphrase of telegram 644.

subfiles.title: Santiago telegram 630
subfiles.about: Possible Japanese gold imports to Chile.
subfiles.summary: Customs recorded only $146 in combined gold and platinum imports through September; inquiries found no evidence of Japanese gold.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Santiago telegram
subfiles.about: Chilean import figures and Japanese vessel arrivals.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrases the customs figures, vessel arrivals at Valparaíso, and negative banking inquiries.

subfiles.title: Copy of Santiago telegram 630
subfiles.about: Chilean checks for Japanese gold shipments.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate telegram reporting no evidence of imports.

subfiles.title: Second paraphrase of Santiago telegram
subfiles.about: Chilean customs data and Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Second paraphrase of telegram 630.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Santiago telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards Santiago telegram 630.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the paraphrase concerning gold imports to Chile.

subfiles.title: Haiti despatch 579
subfiles.from: Edward J. Sparks, American Legation, Port-au-Prince
subfiles.about: Japanese gold and bank credits in Haiti.
subfiles.summary: Reports no gold shipments and a $7,621.47 Yokohama Specie Bank balance from sales of Japanese goods, with no recent withdrawals.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Haiti despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards Haiti despatch 579.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Sparks’s despatch on Japanese gold shipments.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Honduras despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards Honduras despatch 1664.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Tegucigalpa report on gold shipments.

subfiles.title: Honduras despatch 1664
subfiles.from: John D. Erwin, American Legation, Tegucigalpa
subfiles.about: Gold shipments from Japan to Honduras.
subfiles.summary: Reports no recent shipments and notes that Honduran trade with Japan had been at a standstill.

subfiles.title: Guatemala despatch 322
subfiles.from: American Consulate General, Guatemala; Harold Williamson
subfiles.about: Gold shipments and Japanese credits in Guatemala.
subfiles.summary: The central bank reported no gold shipments and one or two frozen commercial credits.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Guatemala despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards Guatemala despatch 322.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the consul general’s report.

subfiles.title: Costa Rica despatch 97
subfiles.from: Leslie E. Reed, American Legation, San José
subfiles.about: Japanese gold shipments to Costa Rica.
subfiles.summary: Two Costa Rican banks reported none recently; the Legation promised to report any future shipments.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Costa Rica despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards Costa Rica despatch 97.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the San José report on Japanese gold.

subfiles.title: Nicaragua despatch 206
subfiles.from: Pierre de L. Boal, American Legation, Managua
subfiles.about: Gold shipments and trade financing in Nicaragua.
subfiles.summary: Financial sources and the National Bank knew of no gold shipments; Japanese firms used dollar letters of credit, and trade was largely compensatory.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Nicaragua despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards Nicaragua despatch 206.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Managua report on Japanese gold.

subfiles.title: Peru despatch 2270
subfiles.about: Japanese gold bullion shipments to Peru.
subfiles.summary: Confirms shipments through the Yokohama Specie Bank to N. Kobayashi and says their value accords with exports to Japan. The Embassy has no concrete evidence of other uses. It asks for a response to Peru’s offer to reject a shipment if the United States considers that helpful.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Peru despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards Peru despatch 2270.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Lima report on Japanese gold bullion.

subfiles.title: Buenos Aires telegram 1377
subfiles.about: Japanese gold received in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: The Central Bank identified one shipment, apparently paying for Argentine exports to Japan.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Buenos Aires telegram
subfiles.about: Argentine account of Japanese gold receipts.
subfiles.summary: Restates that the known shipment paid for merchandise exports, possibly including earlier shipments.

subfiles.title: Treasury transmittal of Buenos Aires telegram
subfiles.about: Forwards Buenos Aires telegram 1377.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the paraphrase concerning Japanese gold in Argentina.

subfiles.title: Timmons memorandum on reported Japanese gold
subfiles.about: British reports of gold aboard the Toa Maru and Azuma Maru.
subfiles.summary: Requests another check on reports of gold discharged in Buenos Aires and Brazil and carried to Callao.

subfiles.title: Currency to be Used in Japanese Areas
subfiles.from: Division of Financial and Monetary Affairs
subfiles.about: Design choices for military currency in Japan and adjacent areas.
subfiles.summary: Sets out decisions needed on the issuing authority’s wording, use of ideographs, and note sizes and colors. Treasury production limits differ from State’s proposals, so the memorandum calls for interdepartmental discussion.

subfiles.title: Comments on military yen design
subfiles.from: Far Eastern and Liberated Areas officials
subfiles.to: Mr. Labouisse; Mr. Reinstein; Mr. Moffat
subfiles.about: Wording, ideographs, sizes, and colors for military yen.
subfiles.summary: Favors neutral wording, bilingual note details, and three size groups.

subfiles.title: Currency design working sheet
subfiles.about: Partly illegible currency-design notes and marks.
subfiles.summary: Two pages of poorly legible notes, characters, and design marks associated with the military currency papers.

subfiles.title: Reinstein letter returning military yen designs
subfiles.about: State Department comments on military yen designs.
subfiles.summary: Requests English and Japanese text, area identification, varied note sizes and colors, and ample small denominations. Reinstein proposes further discussion of production difficulties.

subfiles.title: Copy of comments on military yen design
subfiles.from: Far Eastern and Liberated Areas officials
subfiles.to: Mr. Labouisse; Mr. Reinstein; Mr. Moffat
subfiles.about: Departmental views on military yen.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the April 17 comments on wording, ideographs, and note sizes.

subfiles.title: White transmittal of Netherlands currency correspondence
subfiles.about: Netherlands New Guinea occupation currency and colonial guilder arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Treasury correspondence on Japanese currency and guilder exchange.

subfiles.title: Bell inquiry on Japanese currency
subfiles.about: Treatment of Japanese currency in liberated Netherlands New Guinea.
subfiles.summary: Asks why Japanese currency was declared worthless and how civilians forced to accept it would be treated.

subfiles.title: Crena de Iongh reply on Japanese currency
subfiles.about: Japanese currency found after Hollandia’s liberation.
subfiles.summary: Explains that large quantities of unused or newly seized Japanese notes reached civilians, making exchange impracticable there. Says the Netherlands Indies Government’s stated policy will apply elsewhere where circumstances permit.

subfiles.title: Bell proposal for colonial guilder advances
subfiles.about: Exchange rates for U.S. Army spending in Netherlands territories.
subfiles.summary: Lists four guilder exchange rates and proposes local currency advances with settlement in Washington at an agreed uniform rate.

subfiles.title: Crena de Iongh reply on guilder rates
subfiles.about: Feasibility of a uniform colonial guilder rate.
subfiles.summary: Explains that colonial guilders are distinct currencies, but offers to seek temporary rate uniformity and asks for settlement terms.

subfiles.title: White reply on currency settlement
subfiles.about: Settlement for local currency supplied to U.S. forces.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the proposed dollar settlement arrangement while local agreement is sought.

subfiles.title: Dunn acknowledgment to White
subfiles.about: Acknowledgment of Netherlands currency correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Thanks White for the letters on Japanese currency and guilder exchange.

subfiles.title: CINCPAC request concerning Japanese currency souvenirs
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, Pacific Ocean Areas
subfiles.about: Permission for personnel to retain and transport Japanese currency.
subfiles.summary: Requests authority for personnel to keep up to 20 yen as souvenirs and bring it to Hawaii or the mainland United States.
